reviews.text: This game don't know what he wants to be: an arcade shooter or tactical shooter, it feels like this game is made on roblox. The performance of the game is a bit better than in a playtest but still clunky. a small amount of maps, gunplay is ass. I hope Crowbar Collective will fix this game in the future and make it more enjoyable, but right now it's not good.

While I do enjoy the idea behind the game, it is executed poorly. The roguelike elements are really not even necessary at any point in the game. All the power ups are % increases to speed/armor/damage. Nothing to explore, no builds, just stat padding. First off, the movement and gunplay is extremely jank. You feel slow and wobbly. You are able to lean, but it feels like you are an inflatable waving arm guy in front of a car dealership when doing so. I simply could not get used to it. It plays poorly on a mechanical level and without a complete rehaul of the physics, it is a lost cause. Next, the level design and flow of gameplay. It is once again a low quality job. The enemy units rush at you mindlessly and have massive HP totals. While precision headshots deal more damage, the drunken feeling behind the gun sway, leaning, movement, makes it more frustrating than anything. It's like you are piloting a robot partially made out of jelly. Overall, there is a very limited amount of content. All of it feels vibe coded. There are only a few maps and they have almost no variety between runs. The guns are not impressive and honestly feel boring to shoot due to the lack of the sensation of impact. Guns feel like pellet shooters and trying to aim one makes you feel like a drunk. The game stutters constantly on a 4070 TI, although there are moments where it is smooth. There is some issue with the LoS rendering that hasn't been addressed. Overall, it isn't a long term interest. It's a small game for too much of a price, most of it is probably A.I. Graphics =/= Value Save your money. It barely has 500 players concurrently and it will be dropped inevitably.

I cant bring myself to keep playing this. For the money spent its really not great. Heres what you can expect. - Game cant decide if it wants to make you play it like Payday2 or Ready or Not. A game like that sounds cool but this game does NOT do it well. - Very stiff movement and uncomfortable leaning mechanics. - Unfun and unrewarding gun play. I've straight up seen roblox games do it better. Everything feels stiff, inaccurate, and shoots hit like "Napkins from a kids birthday party" - The characters. Good god please. Just. Shut. UP. I won't go deep into it. Its annoying. Its repetitive. Its bland. You've heard all of these lines before, and in a bad way. The character you play as? Equally if not more annoying. Capture the freeman had better voice acting, and thats not saying much. - The enemies. Payday3 bulldozers, grunts, grunts with snipers, and straight up Borderlands psychos but boring. I cant say much on how the game looks or runs. It looks ight, runs meh. Coming from someone who like stylistic games that aren't just HD graphics n such, this game doesn't reach either side of Looks good - Looks stylish scale. The idea of this game is cool, I like it. But I seriously cannot slog through any more of it. I've gotta get a refund for this, cuz I'm not touching this EVER again. Conclusion? You want a game thats like this but more? Better? Cheaper? Payday 2.
It's really fun solo. Can't really talk about co-op cuz having friends is for casuals.

Game feels absolutely terrible to play. Gunplay feels awful, the gun feels like it never goes where you shoot, I constantly hit walls and geometry. Your gun kicks like a mule so getting accurate shots on enemies is nigh impossible while they beam your head perfectly. Thought maybe a muzzle break and red dot would fix the recoil issue but nope. Red dot jerks around like crazy and it barely visible due to the bright contrasting world. The enemy never misses, it feels like I am playing 1.0 ready or not where the AI will shoot your through a pixel crack in the wall. They also have inhuman reaction time, they will start shooting you perfectly and accurately within like 0.1ms of them seeing a pixel of your shoulder. The enemy constantly knows where you are and will constantly flank you and only peak and push you if you start attacking or looking somewhere else. The lack of consistent self sustain feels awful especially with how unavoidable damage can feel. No armor resupply or ways to replenish your armor (outside of an RNG skill) Enemies don't feel like humans they feel like bots, they know they're disposable and will just walk at you and not be afraid to take damage making impossible to hold any position. The mission types are boring The map layouts can feel like labyrinths, especially on the oil rig. Spending like 10 minutes trying to figure out how to get downstairs after apparently unlocking it from a control panel. Loot rooms that cost the merx phones can sometimes just not have any substantial loot. The whole rouge like aspect to the game feels awful because you feel obligated to commit to a full campaign run but a campaign run can get upwards to an hour and a half. Enemies randomly decide to become bullet sponges despite not having armor. A regular red shirt goes from being a 1 shot with the first pump shotgun you get in the game to 4 or 5 headshots without armor. Feels awful. Enemies are also dead silent, I don't feel like I am playing a coop shooter it feels like I am playing hide and seek. Enemies will legit sit in silence in corners until you peak and start mag dumping you, theres no way of knowing where they are as they don't do any chatter or walk around making footsteps sounds. Speaking of footsteps I don't know if its bugged but I can't hear anyone walking towards me, the exception being the heavies. Any enemy advancing on to me is dead silent and I only know I am being pushed by the fact that I am getting mag dumped point blank. The utility in the game also feels pointless, it feels like it was just put there to feel like a milsim. I saw one point that a ladder could be used and it wasn't even that helpful or save time. The lockpick gun could be used for stealth but the AI has such laser vision stealthing feels impossible. I will get seen from an enemy on the 3rd floor through a bush, through a metal grate and past some fog. Movement also feels sluggish, it feels like I am ice skating and I have bricks on my feet. A million invisible walls on geometry I think I can jump onto or atleast mantle over but can't, an example is the office desks in office. So many issues that just make the game feel jank and unfun. Also the annoying roguelite perk system sucks, most of the perks don't even give you much of a boon/benefit outside of that one perk that allows you to regen armor. Also the selection you get is so limited, getting an actual substantial build going is almost impossible. You could get an explosion perk early on so you think you can spec into throwables except you get a perk later to get closer damage, so shotguns instead? except now you get a perk that increases secondary gun damage. Its awful, no reroll or system to atleast let me buy skills I want. I wanted to like this game but it feels so empty with no meaningful gameplay loop, combat sucks, everything feels jank and I am just not having fun. Too many issues with this game that more content won't fix, the game is broken/unfun from the foundation. TL:DR I don't recommend this game in it's current state

When you play the tutorial you are shown lockpicks, breach charges, sneaking. When you get in game you ignore all of that bc "Aint nobody got time for that!" Timers timers TIMERS! Hurry rush we are running out of time! Timer starts as soon as we spawn in. For what you ask EVERYTHING. Timer to kill elite mercs. Timer to decrypt and steal laptops. Timer for bomb objectives (ok this one gets a pass). Timer for Extraction. Every single level ends in a hoard rush. Some levels are fine because they have cover and choke points to defend. Other maps are literally wide open. enemies can spawn all around you and rush from any direction. or even have level advantage by shooting down at you from towers. Meanwhile you can't go find better cover bc you will fail the extraction. IMO just get rid of this horde rush, use it sparingly OR just let the untouched enemies from the level rush at the end. The 40 extra enemies are tedious when you win and frustrating when you lose. Don't get me started on AMMO... Went into mission with 9mm and 300 extra rounds. Kill merc and pick up his pistol bc it has a sight attached. shot next merc and ran out of ammo. huh? maybe this pistol is a 40 cal or something. go back and pick up the 9mm. back to around 300 rounds. Good. Pick up the 9mm primary gun (mac10 style) from another merc. fight a few more mercs. out of ammo. WHAT??? I have at least 260 9mm rounds left. what do you mean out of ammo? There are bodies all over. guns everywhere. and I'm out of ammo? I'm such a badass that I walk into danger with just a pistol, but my elite training doesn't allow me to remove ammo from downed enemies or unload unused weapons? After some testing- -You drop all ammo reserves if you change weapons. (I R SMRT S-M-R-T!) -Either 9mm Primary and 9mm secondary are different or ammo reserves are stored in the gun itself not your character inventory This game can make some changes and become a good game. This has too many issues right now.

few issues: not sure if the game wants to be a tac shooter or not. the movement, gadgets, and planning all suggest an R63 or SWAT4 style game, but in practice the pace is much faster. timers are strict, and [b]everything is so tanky[/b] including yourself. I ended up for a lot of situations being able to just rely on having really good aim and rushing through everything. I gotta touch on the enemies again. Stealth is not an option solo (despite seeming like the best option for solo). Your starter pistol is completely incapable of 1 tapping even the most basic grunts. the 2nd best option (the Bauer) loses its ability to 1 tap after the first level. Felt like I was, instead of relying on my own wits and planning to finish missions, reliant on RNG skills and dead drop luck. skills are so woefully imbalanced too. first of all, some of which give straight damage upgrades. which is really out of place with the tac shooter pacing the game seems to want(?). there are a few skills that are REQUIRED to be rolled to get a deep run solo. the main ones being armor regen, primary damage and health regen. the armor regen is the ONLY way to get armor back in the entire game. and since each level seemingly has scaling health for all the enemies, the only way to not get outpaced by the AI is to get damage buffs. and since the ambient health pack respawns from the playtest seem to have dissapeared (please buff them again crowbar) passive regen is almost a must. the last major gripe I have is the gunplay. the camera recoil is HORRIBLE, inconsistent, and floaty. for example: the UMP45 has more recoil than a .50AE Desert Eagle. compounded with the really high HP of the enemies and ammo economy being bunk, full auto weapons are never an option. the recoil seems to go vertical and then randomly stop, while the horizontal recoil draws a circle. I think to capture the feel you are looking for you should rebalance recoil per weapon, with the caliber, barrel length and existence of a stock being key factors. the 50AE handcannon should not ever shoot straighter than a 9mm SMG. In short: I highly recommend disabling HP scaling per map, instead changing enemy types as you move forward in the campaign (quick example: changing out the regular grunts slowly into something similar to the squad leader enemy). remove damage scaling perks, and add some features that are perks into the base kit (namely HP regen and some sort of way to replenish armor). Drop the HP of most enemy types slightly, along with buffing their damage so that players need to be more aware of their positioning and in return are able to pick off chaff easier. and please rework the camera recoil (i suggest stealing SWAT's recoil system, with heavy vertical recoil and bloom making up the horizontal recoil). Oh and finally, if you guys decide to stick with the ADS system please both give us another crosshair when we have an optic on, and switch your optics to be parallax based. its already hard to use the ADS system with the camera recoil, having a big red dot thats practically useless after the first shot is a massive hinderance too. If you do decide to pick up this game, first turn off the true ADS setting. then pick up either the Artemis or Bellini and use it until you unlock slugs. slug shotguns are insanely powerful, being able to 1 tap most enemies to the chest while staying VERY accurate. all you need from there is one of the red dots and you are set until the boss fight. I really wish that i will be able to recommend this game very soon. right now its a tough sale with the balance issues and identity crisis. give this one like 3 months though and it could be an insanely fun gem.

你们做的游戏自己玩儿不玩儿？ 先抱怨一波！ 撤离强制守点也就算了，一点防御措施都不给，哪怕你每把撤离阶段空投一波构建防御的物资道具帮助玩家防守撤离也算动脑子了，就凭空让就那么多怪一直被冲，子弹打完了只能被堵在角落里近战打拳还会被ai的动作优先击退。 局内物资供给极度不平衡，缺血药了找到全是给子弹的门，缺子弹了到处血药的门，那个手机开门的设计完全不实用。 ai掉的武器永远没子弹，那我请问他拿头打的我？我子弹没了都不能从ai身上同口径的武器上获取弹药，局内也不给一丁点弹药补给，一个人玩儿纯享折磨，要么缺血药要么缺弹药。 后面的关卡强制兵分两路，老铁，我一个人打，你不动态安排任务目标，让我短时间内拆俩炸弹送俩人质，你当我会分身啊？ 装备系统设计的也很奇怪，防弹衣损耗了不能卖不能扔只能在库存里堆着，也不能花钱修复。 开箱系统设计的目前来说根本不符合这个游戏的规则，只给最烂的东西，毫无用武之地。 ai被瞄准以后战术扭动真的太傻比了，你见过打仗呢谁会在那儿原地扭来扭去像条蛆一样，纯纯是为了恶心人，被爆头了连硬直时间都没有，脑袋都打的爆血雾了还能继续扭来扭去。 游戏潜力很大，但是问题真的也很多很多…… 建议： 撤离问题（局内敌人增援有波次显示，清空所有波次敌人后，撤离不再需要防守等待时间） 物资补给（手机开门可以，但是可以设置成开了门以后玩家自选补给弹药/血药/额外金钱/战术道具，局内有几个玩家就能选几次） ai的武器，就算不拿，也应该有配对的弹药系统可以从ai的尸体或者武器上获取弹药补给或丢弹药给队友，ai的武器即便捡到带回家以后也应该可以正常使用，配件该解锁解锁，别在这种地方做奇怪的限制。 别让ai尬舞了真的太他妈傻逼了，让他们有合作执行战术的思维，而不是在那儿扮演大蛆舞者。 难度变化器 ： 比如， 玩家可以选择轻甲的敌人更多，则敌人的增员波次和敌人的数量则会增加。 选择了重甲敌人更多，则敌人增援的波次和数量则会减少。 玩家选择给敌人更好的武器，则敌人的联合战术进攻的欲望更强烈， 玩家选择给敌人更低伤害的武器，则敌人抱团蹲守任务点的积极性更强烈。 动态难度： 玩家独自一人游玩时，不要在设计多路线的任务目标，因为时间上来说根本来不及，给玩家提供花钱购买的额外战术支援，比如周期性提供敌人位置信息，或者增强玩家的护甲和生命值强度，甚至特殊条件通关后可以解锁花重金购买类似使命召唤的巨力战甲/无畏战士的防御套装组合的购买权，以增强独狼玩家的游戏爽度。 正常流程下，游戏难度应同玩家的游戏进度成正比，而不是后期敌人越强我还是那些破烂什么有用的东西都没有。要么给于玩家同等的增益减益选择空间，要么则把武器装备系统更改为随着游戏难度提升阶段性解锁所有武器装备的使用权而不是花钱，每个玩家可以自选用什么装备组合。（让钱只用于购买各种战术支援和增益减益效果的变动。 现在也只能想到这么多了，以后再玩在思考再提供更多脑洞吧。 补充1： 游戏场景搭建过于暗了，敌人的受击反馈真的不太正常。 是否考虑更多任务时间的选择比如早中晚自定，晚上可以带手电甚至夜视仪。 敌人被击中以后做出更多反应，晕眩→愤怒/怯懦→冲锋/寻找掩体 补充2： 开箱系统更改为玩家选择加倍投入缩减战利品池范围，（并配套对应的战局内增益战术道具战术装备战术支援。）这样前面花小钱解锁一些有点用的小道具，后面难度上去了花大钱抽对玩家实用性更高的各种装备道具或者支援更有意义。而不是给一堆没什么用还能从敌人身上捡到的武器。 补充3： 求求了！别让他被我爆头以后还跟没事儿人似的左右横跳了，我真的害怕！我打的到底是啥？伪人？最好干脆别让他们有这个行为了！ 补充4： 敌人都被打死了，他尸体掉出来的枪还在打我，excuse me？发动技能亡语了？ 补充5：中国风的护甲套装设计的真的很帅！ 补充6：枪械后坐力会导致枪口上台然后挡住瞄准视线看不到敌人的位置了。 补充7：求求了！真的！别让他们被打的时候乱动乱跑了，我真的害怕，全都扎了肾上腺素和止痛药了吗？ 补充8：枪械配件系统不太合理，因为很多枪根本拿不到买不起，更不用说打那么久才能解锁配件了，很多人估计都玩不到解锁配件的时候就已经卸载了，比如说我。或许改成购买模式会更合适一些？（枪械皮肤外观设置为击杀奖励或者特殊条件解锁？） 补充9：瞄准敌人时敌人扭一下这个设定最终导致我卸载了游戏，枪械后坐力很诡异，瞄准了打子弹都打不到人。

It's absolutely an early access game with plenty of rough edges to polish but if you liked terrorist hunt in rainbow six siege, this is fairly similar and will scratch that itch. In it's current state it is annoying to play solo but very enjoyable to play with a friend group. (cough cough) My two largest qualifiers to my friends/complaints to the devs is every mission type bar one ends the exact same way, you get to an extract point and have to hold out against a large portion of enemies. This makes the assault rifle class and high end SMG classes the dominating weapons overall due to their overwhelming DPS and completely removes a lot of the randomness to me as you'll always end up taking the exact same angles to hold off the exact same fights no matter how different the entire level beforehand was. Ideas like skipping the extract if you manage to stealth a whole level or the extract having to suddenly change areas after you arrive would help spice this up a lot. The second is the skills system having three extremely powerful perks. Regenerate HP passively over time, Regenerate armor after kill, and armor durability. If you get all 3 of these you WILL be far more powerful than any other combination out there. I assume the devs that may read this have played payday because of things scattered throughout the game and might even know what i mean when i say it's like getting anarchist and hostage skills without the drawback anarchist normally has of eating your HP. These skills are randomized every run so you may not get this lot of them sometimes but they all feel extremely powerful (especially regenerating armor after kill) and make the rest of them feel quite worthless in comparison. I hope they add more meaningful tools for player power/scaling to add variety or honestly nerf/remove these perks in some way.

[h1] 事前声明 [/h1] 事先声明，我给这款游戏是否推荐点了是 不是因为我推荐这款游戏，而是我相信这款游戏的潜力，我认为它以后会随着更新变得越来越好。但是我不推荐你现在购买这款游戏，最主要的原因就是国区70的原价，打折后仍在50以上，现在来看内容对不起你的定价，如果你能接受这样的定价，那可以接着看下面的优点，你也可以直接跳到后面直接看我说的缺点，但是我说的缺点是个人主观意见，仅供参考。 [h1] 优点很多但无法掩盖明显的缺点 [/h1] [h2] 枪械手感较好，但是仍存在问题 [/h2] 作为一款射击游戏，枪械手感绝对是重中之重，这款游戏枪械手感在我看来属于是打击感较好但是后坐力反馈感较差的一档，手枪，冲锋枪，步枪命中敌人包括爆头时的反馈很明显而且肩射腰射时的准星设计也不是简单的小十字也很有新意，我觉得很有意思手感也很棒，但是霰弹枪效果不佳，霰弹枪的打击感有些软趴趴的而且霰弹枪中还有大傻子打击者这样的经济陷阱枪，不建议使用。后坐力反馈方面会在缺点部分说。 [h2] 肉鸽搭配经济系统FPS，同样的关卡不同技能效果不同经济打法不同 [/h2] 制作组将FPS和肉鸽捏在一起，理论上能够解决大部分同类游戏存在的一个问题“我多打几次背完图，我闭着眼睛都能打”。例如RON就存在这样的问题，因为我也是玩RON玩了很长时间，就是这样的问题，玩的多了知道什么位置大概能出几个就觉得无聊了，没办法重复多次玩，最后只能去打MOD去了。制作组选择加入肉鸽，每局完成给技能，通过技能的搭配做到重复游玩过程不同，起码没那么无聊，经济系统也让玩家游玩时需要多想如何出装，当然了，你们要是把那个大傻子打击者删了更好。 这款游戏的优点肯定还有更多，但是我认为的主要的就是这些，各位肯定也能发掘出其他的。 [h1] 游戏优点明显，缺点也很亮眼 [/h1] [h2] 枪械后坐力反馈存在明显问题，开镜作用微乎其微 [/h2] 后坐力反馈我认为也是枪械手感极为重要的一环，现在存在的问题就是腰射水平散布明显垂直散布几乎没有，开镜设计就反着来，游玩体验大打折扣。正常来说开镜应该是辅助精准射击，但是这款游戏开镜的最大作用是让你不能或者说很难精准射击，首先这款游戏现在没有高倍率瞄具，只有红点换皮红点和全息，AK直接就没有光学瞄具，致敬老手艺射手来了这是。配合我上面说的后坐力反馈问题效果就是AK开镜全自动直接上跳然后枪身挡住视野然后不知道向哪个方向压枪，不如直接腰射。 [h2] 肉鸽元素融合的不算好，通关打法较为死板，通关奖励不尽人意 [/h2] 由于我肉鸽游戏玩的较少，所以如果这部分说的不好请谅解 本游戏的肉鸽由于地图和游玩模式较少的原因，所以在我这对我来说只有技能部分要说，问题在于部分技能就有点毫无作用了，例如摔落伤害降低移速增加和投掷物范围增大，有些技能太过好用导致几乎是必选，例如杀敌回复护甲。 我现在单通战役已经不成问题，主要就是因为单人打法死板，多人由于有队友增加容错，所以在技能选择方面可以随性一点，但是单人很难，单人前期就是尽可能用200块的P320攒经济吃技能，尽早出杀敌回复护甲的技能然后买大甲开始猛攻，如果随不出杀敌回甲，那单通难度很高，因为这游戏的甲能够有一定的减伤效果，后期如果不带甲，小兵刮死人很简单。如果你随机技能每次都是摔落伤害移速和投掷物，那你要坐牢了，本来移速是有用的，但是撤离点守点机制会给你上一课。 通关奖励方面，我个人喜欢把肉鸽的通关奖励分为两种，一种是能带进对局增加能力的硬奖励，例如属性提升，概率提高等。一种是没有实际提升，但是纯好看的软奖励，例如皮肤，装饰，特效等。而这游戏的软奖励在我看来其实一般，枪械皮肤大多是简单换色缺少新意，人物皮肤相较于枪械皮肤来说较好，但是仍然差的很多，人物模型缺少力量感，其实完全可以参考GIGN这类的出重甲配大头盔把人整个装在里面看起来观感还能好不少。至于硬奖励，只有枪械需要多次完成战役解锁，但是其实你不解锁也不耽误你单通战役，单通全程理论上只需要P320和一把N4即可，没有N4使用4400块的M16其实也可以，没有配件也能打，不过难度稍高。所以对我来说通关结果就是解锁一把或两把枪，试一试发现多少有点垃圾，然后再也不玩了，这里点名大傻子打击者。 [h2] 敌人索敌机制奇怪，交火时敌人的移动体验差，投掷物设计不好，撤离点守点机制讨厌，配合机场地图更是新人必吃榜首 [/h2] 敌人的索敌机制在我看来多少有些逆天了，每次打死一名敌人他周围的会直接锁定打死敌人的玩家，而且无视地形遮蔽，难道你们真有框？有框不看是演队友是吧。然后稍微距离远一点的敌人熟视无睹，看见了尸体也不管，队友开枪也不问，何意味？你开演了是吧，你Rating不红谁红？然后子弹但凡在他侧边擦一下马上锁人，这不是演员这是啥。 敌人在和玩家交火时会频繁地进行较为快速的左右横向移动，导致我在游玩时我很容易马枪，这种移动方式让我想起了RON的厕所战神赵维克，配合优化差导致的突然掉帧，一个敌人很有可能就直接挂掉你的甲甚至直接打残玩家。 投掷物敌人搭配上面说的直接就是队友一死看你一眼一个闪光弹上来，投掷物还带锁，只要上方没有障碍物不可能扔歪，闪光弹在一定距离内你背闪也是吃满的效果，确实很真实，就是有点破坏游戏体验了。 正常关卡结束前会有一个撤离守点的过程，这个过程很多敌人冲点，玩家需要守点拖时间，但是问题是机场地图撤离点范围过小还是处于高地，敌人出口距离撤离点太近而且是前后分布的，导致单人守点几乎不可能，只需要对面一颗闪配合一个重甲兵一个近战两个方向冲你就能给很大压力，我单通时候机场直接就不选，如果你能单人守难度2和3的机场撤离点，那你确实很厉害。 [h1] 优化问题和一些小BUG以及我对制作组的期望 [/h1] 优化问题主要体现在游玩时会出现突然的掉帧很影响对枪时候的瞄准，开镜问题可以通过游戏内置选项中有一个放大视野代替开镜视角来规避，再就是格洛克在检视是存在使用长弹匣检视时变成短弹匣的BUG。 从我的角度来看，肉鸽配FPS非常好玩，但是也很难做平衡，毕竟FPS要求真实的话枪爆头必须要击杀，而且也有很多问题我在这里也没有说明，例如地图资源分配问题，部分关卡存在的怪堵梯子问题，如何平衡娱乐性和真实性。但是这些问题都是制作组需要仔细考虑多次测试才能解决的，所以我选择相信制作组，我也希望制作组能把这款游戏做好，没做好也没关系，我到时候再写个差评就好了。

Having played this, I have to say I expected more from Rogue Point. Maybe it’s because I’ve played other Rogue-like/Rogue-lite titles like MythForce or Roboquest, which nail the genre perfectly, but I’m just not feeling it here. It’s likely because the game reuses the same 4 maps over and over with minimal changes, probably in the name of "realism." On the positive side, I actually enjoyed the gameplay loop. Managing your budget for loadouts each round, the gunplay, the feeling of being armored up, and the unpredictability of what enemies will appear in the next level. What bums me out, though, is that the game is clearly designed for groups. Playing solo is much harder, especially since you have to buy your weapons, so forget about starting with an AK. There’s also a lack of maps and the current player base is so small that it’s nearly impossible to find a match. I really hope that once the game leaves Early Access, It’ll be a total banger.

I'll give them this: it's still early access. However I've got issues with the state of the game at the moment and I hope this negative review will get back to the devs as feedback. Firstly the things i like: I like the gunplay, i like the dynamic crosshair that resembles your actual sights/optics, makes me feel like ADS is a suggestion and not compulsory. I like how headshots are practically 1 tap across all weapons, with limited exceptions. Here's where I start to not like some things. Firstly, map diversity. There's only 4 maps which... fair... early access, but even those 4 maps get old fast. The randomization of each map (such as isolating certain parts of the map, etc) doesnt do enough to make each map feel fresh every time i load into it. At the moment it feels like i'm loading the exact same map, except the magical dice that decide where all the interactable stuff is has rolled a 4 instead of a 5. Some of the maps are really difficult to navigate. Oil Rig seems to be the biggest issue, with limited paths between the upper levels and the moon pool, and some of those being frequently blocked based on the objectives. There's very limited replayability at the moment. The only persistent progression at the moment seems to be the player's cosmetics (unlocked by completing campaigns) and the attachments/skins to the player's guns (new items unlocked by using the guns and getting kills/headshots). There isn't really much reason to play the game beyond a few hours because that's literally the entire game - complete a campaign and you've basically played the entire game's content in one sitting, the question from here is "who else can i play with" or "can i make this session more interesting by arbitrarily restricting myself to X weapon or Y type of gun". There's no incentive from the developers to have the player return to the game after already playing a campaign. All in all, for an early access title, it's ok. But before it hits full release I'm hoping to see some of the following - More Maps (think never playing the same map twice in a single campaign) - Greater levels of variety between each map (what if each map had several layouts you could play on? maybe a version of office where there are two smaller buildings instead of one larger one?) - Persistent progression that doesnt subtract from the rogue-like aspects of the game. Not sure what this would look like. Maybe you could rework the dead drop system so that dead drops become items you get to use across multiple campaigns (provided you didnt lose them) - More "final mission" variety. Its kinda boring when the "final mission" is just "kill this bullet sponge". Can we get some variety? Maybe a "death run" where you and your party must rush through a makeshift obstacle course filled with traps, locked doors, and enemies to get to the extract? I'm not too sure, but the same bullet sponge mission every time gets boring. - Make merx stashes actually worth opening. I've opened dozens of them, but i've found that unless its a dead drop stash, its a complete waste of time. The gun stash will usually only have a secondary (or worse, literally the same gun I already have), the only time I found something useful outside of that is when i've opened a medic stash while low on HP. The value of these stashes needs to be improved.

Clunky, awkward, and a bit obtuse. Since the game and I had so much in common I thought it might be a shoe in, but also similarly to me it lacks depth, polish, and literally any reason to play the game after you've finished 1 campaign. Guns do not feel great, have janky animations, are wildly inaccurate to where you are aiming, and seemingly random damage. (An AK that one-taps one guy to the dome can turn to the dude 1m to his right and take 3 shots to the head to kill him. They are both not wearing head armor.). They also have horrible sound design, mechanical design, feeling, and recoil. They tried to do the 'height over bore' thing where your gun shoots from the barrel, but they seem to have done something horribly wrong because your gun shoots from about 3 inches below where your barrel actually is- So if something is say, 30% below your eyeline, you can't shoot over it, even if your gun is visibly over the top of the object. Enemies are both blind and precognizant. Able to see you through a wall perfectly fine, but if you stand in front of them it's a 50/50 chance they'll notice in my experience. There is SOME variety. Guys with pistols who die in one shot to the head, guys with revolvers who die in one shot to the head but will flashbang you first, guys with SMGs who will die in one shot to the head, guys with SMGs who won't die in one shot to the head but are not visually different to those who will, guys with machetes who are buck naked and yet take more damage than guys wearing actual body armor, shotgun guys, shotgun guys with armor, snipers, guys with rifles who look like the guys with pistols and guys with smgs but seemingly die in random amounts of shots to the head.. This doesn't feel like early access. This feels like something that is so drastically unfinished that it shouldn't have been released yet. There are issues here that feel so fundamental that it's not an issue of 'some balance changes' but more like needing to rewrite entire systems. Maybe they'll fix some of these issues, but some others I do not see getting fixed unless the game has major overhauls and I can only assume if they are going to be addressed are going to take a very long time to do so. If you want something to kill a few hours and then not touch for 2 years, this is your game. Otherwise, I cannot recommend. It's got potential, but still needs time in the oven. I don't recommend it YET. First off, the game has a terrible identity crisis - on one hand it seems like it wants to be a realistic military shooter, but then it completely breaks that by dropping wacky machete-wielding fiends who charge you head-first. I'd suggest leaning a bit into the wacky vibe, with more weird enemies, gear and upgrades, because the realistic shooter market is a bit oversaturated at the moment. Despite the satisfying feel of the weapons, the gunplay feels... odd. Weapons do nothing to armored enemies, except for hitting an unarmored headshot, which instantly takes them down. This makes weapons of the same type feel really same-ish, with only minor differences. When I bought this game, I expected the map to feel completely different with each run, since the store page talked so extensively about the systems for exactly that purpose, but in its current iteration you can really easily learn the maps, with the changes being pretty minor. So far, the Mall map seems to be the most varied, while the Airport (despite being my favourite) seems least random. Some maps really suffer from having tiny crevices or decorations (like plants) that enemies can see you through, even though you cannot see them. Makes the whole experience really annoying. The balance of the skills is also relatively wack, with some of them being must-haves (health on kill, armor on kill, passive regen) and some of them being either useless or just boring - I don't recall ever being excited by bonus SMG reload speed... The voice acting suffers from a serious case of "Focus, M"-type dialogue. I don't think I need to elaborate more on that. With time, I could see this game turning into a brilliant masterpiece, but right now, I wouldn't call this a good purchase, especially for its price.

I try to be open minded when playing EA titles. While I'm excited to see what Rogue Point has to offer in the future, I can't help but feel off about the gameplay in its current state. The most glaring issue is this: Bots CAN and WILL shoot you before even being able to properly acknowledge you. You can see them pulling the trigger mid-turn as they face you. They will attempt to shoot you through metal doors because you tapped sprint. They will shoot you as their shoulder is just being revealed around the corner. All of these situations hitting you about 80% of the time, resulting in runs feeling rather unfair. In the context of the rogue-lite gameplay loop, it's very debilitating. Things might be more balanced for group play, but as for solo I would give it some more time to cook.

[b]It's like Ready or Not but for those who aren't into RP or the accompanying bitter aftertaste of pork. [/b] Rogue Point is an interesting experience, very much inspired by games like SWAT and aformentioned Ready or Not, but with less gritty realism of law enforcement scenarios and more focus on intense action gunfights. It still has teamplay, pre-mission planning, methodical movement and combat encounters, and impactful gunplay but without feeling subtly fascist as you gun down your target. The meta is also approached differently, having roguelike missions with elements of meta progression though weapon use (attachments), skill upgrades, and character and weapon cosmetic customisation. It's a bit rough, but it's reasonably priced and a lot of fun. Overally I recommend it, especially for those who are interested in the core gameplay and teamplay aspects that go with tactical shooters but want something a bit more casual and less focused on law enforcement simulation. [i]Disclaimer: I am playing this game on a free weekend and have not yet purchased it myself.[/i]

Man... this one is a tough call because it's a genuinely fun experience BUT a very confused one. The mechanics of the game, its visuals and gameplay COMPLETELY CLASH against each other. Features like cracking doors open, leaning, optiwands etc. have no space to shine in a game where snappy aim, bunny hopping and sprinting everywhere are BY FAR the best way to beat each level. It is my humble opinion that the devs should first decide what this game is meant to be, truly, because there's some tactical elements similar to games like Ready or Not and Zero Hour that can just be overlooked completely. I don't mind when games aren't too serious in their design or art style, but there comes a point when it just gets annoying. In this game, that came through with voice acting. The enemy chatter on radios is constant, often nonsensical and the player operators are just infuriating to listen to. After each kill your character will have a dumb remark to throw at the enemy or you'll hear "We will rock you!" like eight times within a minute. I personally love the progression aspect and I hope they expand upon those systems further. The gunplay, while undoubtably janky, was fun and rather satisfying. Where the experience falls short is with animations and sounds, just all around, 3rd person animations and most weapon sfx need a complete overhaul. To sum it up, Crowbar Collective, REALLY think about the kind of experience that you wish to bring, there is SO MUCH POTENTIAL but as it stands currently it's just a big mess of mechanics and design choices that don't work well together... at least not with how they're currently implemented. Make the game punish carelessness more, tone down how mobile players are, make those "tactical" features shine a bit more and for the love of God hire a few more voice actors... matter of fact, just rewrite all the dialogue while at it, it's so cringe at the moment... especially the player operators.

This is a review of the game from a solo player. I would like to start off by saying if you are not sure about this game watch the gameplay trailer and the reveal trailer on the store page. They should be the two in the very back. I personally found them to be the best depictions of the game rather than the other trailers that seem to lean more into the goofy side of things. While the game is balanced for coop, playing solo is a lot of fun and very doable. You just have to have more caution and planning. I find it very satisfying being outnumbered and pulling off a mission despite the odds. GAME DESCRIPTION I think the game is a very good mix of arcade shooter and tactical shooter that makes it very easy to pickup and play for a couple of hours at a time without feeling like a chore to play. I think the best way to describe this game is its like a mix of Rainbow Six T hunt, Counter-Strike, and Payday. CONTENT For me personally I think the amount of content available right now is enough to justify the price and even better if you get the game on sale. It has a lot of guns and unlocks for each weapon that I find a lot of fun playing multiple playthroughs to unlock everything. Not to mention the cosmetics for your operator look fantastic. I have seen some people say that the guns feel the same but I find that the sound design alone makes every gun feel unique and satisfying to use. I will say that as of now there are only three locations but to my understanding more are gonna be added later and what is available I think is pretty good. BUGS So far the only bugs I have run into are things like some shots being blocked by what appears to be invisible objects and foot steps of enemies sounding closer than they really are. But I imagine that things will get fixed with time. CONCLUSION I think the game is very fun and worth the price. Honestly if the devs were to just stop working on the game I would still be satisfied with my purchase. I don't review games on Steam but I love this game a lot and hope more people give it a try. I apologize if my review is a little all over the place again, I don't leave reviews like ever but I will go a ahead and end things off with a few tips for any solo players who might want to try the game out. TIPS FOR SOLO PLAYERS 1. User cover and choke points. 2. Use Smokes they help a lot during extraction phase. 3. Suppressors help a lot. 4. This game is very confusing. It tries to treat itself like a tactical shooter in the vein of SWAT 4 and Ready or Not, with there being all of these tactical equipment designed to disrupt and predict your enemies. The problem is that the core gameplay does not support this playstyle at all since it's basically a run and gunner. Enemies are not a threat by themselves, instead they just mob you like crazy (spawning literally behind you sometimes), and have basic AI. Compare this to SWAT where, while the AI was still not crazy, they were an actual threat. A single dude in that game can put you down very quickly, which alongside the slow pacing of the game, made you have to act tactically. Predicting and planning around the enemy was actually important since they were a threat that occupied space. In Rouge Point the enemies aren't a serious threat by themselves, they don't really occupy space since they will just swarm you, and the game pace is so fast that you don't need to be tactical. It's just better (and feels better) to rush enemies and shoot them like you're playing a crappy counter strike custom level. I still enjoy the game, but I think for most people this is the worst of both worlds. The run and shoot gameplay is ok, but not strong enough to carry the simple gameplay loop. The tactical gameplay doesn't really matter since you don't need to plan at all. Planning just slows the game down without much pay off. The writing is also whatever, with the general vibe being that there's no identity to the game. It's not bad, it's just that there's literally nothing there. Still, if you're just looking for cheap shooter, it's alright. I don't mind the issues that much, but I think for most people there are games that focus on parts of this one that are more enjoyable.
